metadata.title: Growth mindset mediates perceptions of teachers' and parents' process feedback in digital reading performance: Evidence from 32 OECD countries

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata from 32 OECD countries and applies the final student weight recommended by PISA (W_FSTUWT) to obtain unbiased population parameter estimates. The analytic sample is restricted to students with available data for the variables of interest (digital reading literacy PV1READ, growth mindset item, TEACHSUP, EMOSUPS, and controls). The authors do not report replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), but they do explicitly state the use of W_FSTUWT in the multilevel mediation/SEM framework. Because the analysis is SEM-based rather than tree/boosting ML, the paper does not discuss ML-specific weight omission; instead it follows PISA guidance for weighted generalization.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 (computer-based) reading assessment data for students in 32 OECD countries whose data were available for the study’s variables of interest (digital reading literacy PV1READ, growth mindset item, TEACHSUP, EMOSUPS, and controls). Students were randomly assigned to different electronic test forms; scores were scaled using IRT and the dependent variable was defined using the first plausible value draw (PV1READ). Missing values were imputed for five continuous variables using the EM algorithm; student gender was complete and excluded from imputation. The multilevel mediation model was run separately for each country, with students nested within schools and schools nested within countries.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (digital reading literacy), OECD 32 countries
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel mediation/SEM path coefficients (standardized β) reported by country: total effects TEACHSUP β range 0.027–0.134 (20 countries significant); total effects EMOSUPS β range 0.027–0.200 (30 countries significant). Control effects: Student gender βs range −0.504 to −0.088; ESCS βs range 0.089–0.280. Mediation: growth mindset path b β range 0.074–0.392 (all countries significant).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (digital reading literacy PV1READ) from 32 OECD countries, the study leveraged teacher process feedback, parent process feedback, student gender, and ESCS to predict digital reading literacy, finding that both TEACHSUP and EMOSUPS had small but statistically significant positive total effects in most countries and that growth mindset significantly predicted digital reading performance (path b βs up to 0.392). This indicates that strengthening process-oriented feedback from both teachers and parents—while fostering students’ growth mindset—may support improvements in adolescents’ digital reading achievement, though the results are correlational and not causal.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (digital reading literacy), OECD 32 countries
main_findings.performance_metrics: Direct effects on growth mindset (path a1 and a2): TEACHSUP significant in 18 countries with β range 0.029–0.095; EMOSUPS significant in 24 countries with β range 0.027–0.161. Indirect effects via growth mindset: TEACHSUP→GM→PV1READ (a1b) β range 0.003–0.019; EMOSUPS→GM→PV1READ (a2b) β range 0.003–0.027. Proportion mediated: teacher path 4.8%–53.6% (18 countries); parent path 2.8%–46.8% (25 countries).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data from 32 OECD countries, the study leveraged teacher and parent process feedback (with gender and ESCS controls) to predict students’ growth mindset, finding that perceived process feedback significantly promoted growth mindset in a majority of countries (TEACHSUP significant in 18/32; EMOSUPS in 24/32) and that growth mindset mediated the feedback–digital reading relationship with proportion mediated often exceeding 10%. This indicates that policy and practice should prioritize process-focused feedback practices that students perceive from both school and home contexts to cultivate growth-oriented beliefs that translate into better digital reading outcomes, while recognizing that the mediation is based on cross-sectional associations.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2018 computer-based reading data for 32 OECD countries (N=250,912 students from 9,923 schools). The dependent variable is digital reading literacy measured via plausible values, using only PV1READ, and the mediator is a single-item growth mindset treated as continuous. The authors estimate multilevel mediation/SEM models separately by country, applying the PISA final student weight W_FSTUWT and imputing missing values for five continuous variables using the EM algorithm. Results show small but significant total effects of teacher process feedback and parent process feedback on digital reading literacy in most countries, and growth mindset significantly predicts digital reading performance (path b βs up to 0.392). Mediation effects vary cross-nationally, with teacher-path mediation proportion ranging 4.8%–53.6% and parent-path 2.8%–46.8%. Limitations include correlational interpretation (no causal identification) and the use of a single-item growth mindset measure.
